subject: Civic Education
lesson: Expresses the ability to face problems in day-to-day life should be developed: Citizen-Officer Deliberation Roleplay: Competency Level 8.5.1
unique_learning_outcome: Expresses the ability to face problems in day-to-day life should be developed.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: The teacher writes or reads “Expresses the ability to face problems in day-to-day life should be developed” and asks students to name one example they have seen in everyday life. Students share brief responses; the teacher connects their examples to Citizen-Officer Deliberation Roleplay: Competency Level 8.5.1 and explains how it will help them explore this period's outcome.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: Teacher organizes students into structured inquiry teams and introduces the task scenario.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students review task cards, assume collaborative group roles, and begin investigations.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: Teacher moderates student presentations, highlights key points, and addresses misconceptions.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Student spokespersons present findings, compare observations, and note feedback.

summary: Consolidation and synthesis of key concepts: Students reflect on their roleplay experience and how it relates to real-life problems and challenges.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Final closure formative assessment criteria: Students' roleplay decisions and reasons are evaluated for understanding of the importance of facing problems and challenges in day-to-day life.
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: Each student completes a short exit response explaining one finding about “Expresses the ability to face problems in day-to-day life should be developed” using evidence or an example from Citizen-Officer Deliberation Roleplay: Competency Level 8.5.1. The teacher reviews responses for an accurate link to the period outcome.
selected_activity:
Activity: Citizen-Officer Deliberation Roleplay: Competency Level 8.5.1
Approach: Students use citizen-officer deliberation roleplay to explore 'Expresses the ability to face problems in day-to-day life should be developed.'. Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (35 students): Desks arranged into 7 teams (7 teams (7 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Student task: Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (35 students): Desks arranged into 7 teams (7 teams (7 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Teacher facilitation: Organizes all 35 students using 7 teams (7 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer. and monitors progress with outcome-focused prompts and time checks. Circulates across 7 teams, facilitating role execution and formatively checking progress.
Expected output: A short role-based civic decision and its reasons.
Grouping: 7 teams (7 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer.
